text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
* Prime minister Romano Prodi said the European Union summit held in Amsterdam on Monday might have boosted Italy's chances of joining Europe's single currency from the start (all).
* Centre-right opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi said he was ready to find a compromise with majority coalition about the two-round electoral system (all).

* Fiat group chiarman Cesare Romiti said the Italian industrial group's sales in the first five months of this year rose 8.2 percent to 1.12 million units. Romiti also said the group's April results were "considerably above those in April last year" and May should also show favourable results. He saw a 9.0 trillion lire rise in the group's auto sales for 1997. Romiti also confirmed he was going to leave office in 1998 (all).

* Shareholders in Italian state industrial holding IRI approved the appointment of a new board which includes new chairman Gian Maria Gros-Pietro (all). In an interview, Gros-Pietro said his target was the sell-off of all IRI's activities in three-year's time (La Repubblica).

* A report by national statistics institute Istat showed Italian producer prices rose 0.8 percent in April compared with a rise of 0.9 percent in March and of 2.6 percent in April 1996. Istat report also showed Italian wholesale price fell 0.7 percent in April against a rise of 0.3 percent in March and an increase of 4.5 percent in April 1996 (Sole 24 ore).

* Bank of Italy governor Antonio Fazio said Europe was lagging behind in structural reforms necessary to compete effectively on global markets. Fazio also said economic globalisation risked leading to inflation and currency speculation unless individual countries coordinated policies and strengthened their economies (all).
**Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
